ai.title: Lazy four-ad pool for inline CLI response ads
ai.summary: Inline response ads in the CLI assistant now use a lazily filled four-ad pool (`MAX_RESPONSE_AD_POOL_SIZE` = 4) instead of a per-prompt batch auction. The new `cli/src/utils/lazy-response-ads.ts` module serializes one ad fetch per newly eligible slot via `requestLazyResponseAds`, keyed by assistant message id, and `getResponseAdForSlot` repeats that stable pool for later slots without extra auctions or impression events. `RESPONSE_AD_NODE_STEP` in `cli/src/utils/response-ad-positions.ts` drops from 4 to 2, so an ad slot becomes eligible after every other rendered node instead of every fourth. `AdCard` gains an `inline` variant with a compact three-row layout from `getInlineAdLayout`, and `allowInlineAds` metadata is set on new answer shells and stripped on restored messages so ads are never retroactively fetched into settled history.
ai.evidence: New file cli/src/utils/lazy-response-ads.ts exports `createLazyResponseAdQueue`, `requestLazyResponseAds`, `getResponseAdForSlot`, `responseAdDisplayCount`, `MAX_RESPONSE_AD_POOL_SIZE` (4); hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts imports them and removes the per-prompt batch auction (`ADS_PER_PROMPT`=8, `computeResponseAds`, `drawUnusedAd`, `PromptAdBatch`, `isPromptMessage`); cli/src/components/blocks/blocks-renderer.tsx calls `onResponseAdsNeeded` when eligible slots grow and renders `AdCard` with `variant="inline"` using `getResponseAdForSlot`.
ai.migration: If you are building custom ad renderers against the CLI, replace `ads[0]`-based inline rendering with the `onResponseAdsNeeded` callback and pass `variant="inline"` to `AdCard`.
ai.unknowns: The production consumer of the `CLI-Chat-Inline` placement id and whether the server-side auction honors the serialized per-slot ordering.

ai.title: SDK run-terminal-command adds MSYS disablepcon on Windows
ai.summary: run-terminal-command.ts appends disable_pcon to MSYS env var on Windows. Prevents Git Bash descendants from allocating ConPTY despite detached/hidden flags. Preserves existing MSYS options via filter/join. Scope: SDK terminal tool.

eli5.text: If you're using the SDK on a Windows computer and the program launches a terminal window (for example, when it tries to run something in the background), it now quietly tells a helper named MSYS to turn off a modern display mode called ConPTY. That mode was causing Git Bash (a common terminal tool) to pop up a visible window even when the program asked for it to stay hidden, so this change keeps your screen from flashing that window and also makes sure any other settings you already configured for that helper are still kept intact. The change is live today and applies automatically whenever the program starts a shell command on Windows.

In `cli/src/chat.tsx` the header is now wrapped in a `box` with a `headerRef` and `isHeaderVisible` state, so the sheen animation driven by `useSheenAnimation` is gated on viewport visibility rather than running unconditionally. eli5.text: When you chat with the assistant and a response streams in, small banner ads used to be fetched in one big batch of eight before your reply. Now the system first collects a smaller, capped pool of four unique ads, only showing them once they've fully loaded, and then quietly cycles through that same stable set to fill each available ad slot, so you still get ads woven between your reply sections, just without waiting on a large upfront load. The ad slots now turn on or off based on how many response sections you have (every two sections earns one non-trailing slot), and the team added two new usage stats that record when an inline ad slot became eligible and when a previously built ad pool got reused. This is live today: the desktop client now reads these helpers from the shared package, so
